tagline: A slow loop around Lake Waramaug, and back to the falls.
intro: Out of New Preston, Route 45 runs a half mile through the village and comes out on the east shore of Lake Waramaug. From there an unsigned state road, SSR 478, carries on around the south, west and north shores, so the drive becomes a slow loop past houses, seasonal cottages and boathouses on a shore that is nearly all private.

The lake is a natural one, raised by a small concrete and masonry dam, and 40 feet at its deepest. It drains south into the East Aspetuck River, which takes the water back through New Preston and over the falls.

moments.title: New Preston
moments.text: The East Aspetuck runs through the village center and over New Preston Falls, in country of steep hills, narrow valleys and ledge rock.

moments.title: Lake Waramaug State Park
moments.text: On the northwest shore is the lake's one public way to the water, a park the state began buying in 1920, with swimming, camping and a launch for canoes.

moments.title: Marbledale
moments.text: Out along US 202, a village that kept a prosperous cooper's shop in the 19th century and has kept St. Andrew's Episcopal Church, Gothic Revival, since 1822.
